key_insight: CNN and SVC achieved high reported accuracy in MRI brain tumor classification, with CNN performing best on the larger benchmark dataset.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support MRI-based tumor assessment, but these research results do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Compared six feature representations, including LBP, Gabor filters, wavelets, Fourier transforms, CNN features, and run-length matrices.
Evaluated k-nearest neighbor, random forest, SVC, probabilistic neural network, and CNN classifiers.
Used statistical tests to assess LBP features and SHAP to explain feature contributions.
evidence_signal: Reported accuracy was 97.8% for CNN and 98.06% for SVC on a small dataset, versus 98.9% and 96.7%, respectively, on a larger benchmark dataset.
watch_item: The abstract does not report dataset sizes, patient-level splitting, or external clinical validation, limiting assessment of generalizability.
paper_title: Enhanced MRI brain tumor detection using deep learning in conjunction with explainable AI SHAP based diverse and multi feature analysis
